sections.h2: Clark County offices for Vancouver owners
sections.html:
Vancouver houses are taxed by Clark County. The Treasurer, the Assessor and the Board of Equalization all work from the Public Service Center, 1300 Franklin Street, downtown. Values come from the Assessor, statements and payments from the Treasurer, and appeals go before the Board.

  • Treasurer: 564.397.2252, treasoff@clark.wa.gov, second-floor Joint Lobby. Walk-in hours are Monday to Thursday, nine in the morning to four in the afternoon. Phone and email help is offered on Fridays as well, until 4:30 in the afternoon.
  • Assessor: 564.397.2391, assessor@clark.wa.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: Suite 650, 564.397.2337, BOE@clark.wa.gov.

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, on the north bank of the Columbia River across from Portland. It had 199,698 residents in July 2025 on 48.74 square miles of land. Owners occupy 50.8 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $462,400, median gross rent is $1,702 and median household income is $81,338.

Not every Vancouver mailing address is inside the city. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek are unincorporated communities just north of the city limits. The county's Property Information Center will show whether your parcel is in the city, and the levies shift with the tax area.

For 2026 the county's levy report puts the total at $9.6856 per $1,000 of assessed value in tax area 037000, which covers the City of Vancouver and Vancouver School District 37. Other tax areas inside the city carry different district combinations, so trust the rate on your own statement.

Spring brings the first-half deadline, April 30, and that is also the date for anyone paying the full year at once. The fall deadline is October 31. A mailed check counts only if the Postal Service postmarks it that same day, so the county advises handing it to a post office clerk and avoiding the collection box. E-check payments online are free. Expect first-half statements around March 15 and second-half statements around September 15.

For tax years 2023 and later, a residential parcel of four or fewer units is charged 0.75 percent a month and no penalty. Everything else is billed 1 percent monthly and adds a 3 percent penalty on June 1, then 8 percent on December 1.

  • Chapter 84.64 RCW lets the county foreclose on real property once three or more years of tax are unpaid.
  • After court proceedings begin, all taxes, interest, penalties and foreclosure costs must be paid in full before the auction.
  • After a certificate of delinquency is filed, only owners and recorded interests can make payments to the Treasurer.
  • Owner-occupants who qualify by income and face foreclosure may ask once for interest and penalties to be waived under RCW 84.56.020(19).

The Treasurer's office is the right first call for a payoff figure, and nothing about a pending sale stops you from paying a delinquent year early. If you are behind, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov or call 564.397.2252 before you list the home.

sections.h2: Does your mortgage escrow pay Vancouver property tax?
sections.html:
More than 45 percent of Clark County homeowners pay through escrow. For those owners the county sends no statement, and you stay responsible for confirming each installment was actually paid.

Lenders occasionally pay the wrong account number or skip a payment. After April 30 and October 31, open the taxes tab on the Property Information Center and check. If a delinquency notice shows up, ask the lender which account numbers it paid and request a cancelled check or disbursement record. Confirm with the lender before sending your own money, because paying twice is a real risk.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Vancouver property value
sections.html:
Your window is 60 calendar days from the date printed on the Notice of Value, or July 1 if that comes later, and the appeal goes to the county's equalization board. Late appeals cannot be accepted, and the 60 days are counted from the notice date, not as two months. You may also file a preemptive appeal anytime from January 1 through July 1 of the assessment year.

Most Notices of Value go out in June and the rest in September, and only properties whose value changed receive one. Filing is free. A three-member citizen board hears each case in about 15 minutes and mails a written decision within 30 days. Historically, more than half of appeals end well for the owner, either after a talk with the Assessor or at the hearing.

  • Strongest evidence: comparable sales or a recent appraisal, repair bids and photographs.
  • Other properties' assessed values do not persuade the board.
  • Extra evidence has to reach the Board 21 business days before the hearing.
  • If you disagree with the result, the State Board of Tax Appeals is the next stop.

Clark County's senior exemption uses three income tiers. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the top income limit is $62,000, and for 2027 through 2029 it rises to $85,000 under Senate Bill 6162. Applicants for 2027 need to be 61 or older, unable to work due to disability, or rated 40 percent or higher for a service-connected disability. They must also own the home and occupy it at least six months of the year. Applications for 2027 open in February 2027, and current participants are adjusted automatically.

At closing, RCW 84.60.020 attaches the tax lien on January 1 and, without a contract term, divides the year by the sale date. Ask your escrow officer to confirm both halves with the Treasurer, and ask the Assessor whether an exemption or deferral ends with the sale.

Before you put a Vancouver house on the market, spend ten minutes with the statement. Each bill lists the taxes from every district, and the county's lookup shows whether anything is delinquent.

  • Confirm the tax area number, since it decides the rate.
  • Check both halves as paid, especially if a lender handles escrow.
  • See whether an exemption is on the account, and learn from the Assessor what stops when you sell.
  • If a balance is open, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov for a payoff before the buyer's title company asks.

With a cash buyer there is no lender reviewing taxes, yet the title company still checks the record and anything owed is taken from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Vancouver, WA property tax due?
faqs.a: Spring and fall: April 30 covers the first half or the full year, and October 31 covers the second half. Statements are usually ready by March 15 and September 15.

faqs.q: What interest does Clark County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: A residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 0.75 percent monthly with no penalties, for tax years 2023 and later. Everything else pays 1 percent monthly and picks up the June 1 and December 1 penalties of 3 and 8 percent.

faqs.q: How long before Clark County forecloses for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Three years. Real property with taxes three or more years delinquent can be foreclosed. Call the Treasurer at 564.397.2252 or email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov to discuss relief.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Vancouver?
faqs.a: Sixty calendar days counted from the mailing date of your Notice of Value, unless July 1 is later. Late appeals cannot be accepted. Reach the Board of Equalization at 564.397.2337 or BOE@clark.wa.gov.

faqs.q: Is my Vancouver address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek sit north of the city limits and are unincorporated. The Clark County Property Information Center shows which tax area applies to your parcel.
